modality_context: KO (Shifrut/Marson primary human CD8 T-cell CRISPR-KO screens); concordance rule: concordant = protective_lof
io_rationale: Suppressor of cytokine signaling; brakes JAK/STAT + TCR. KO enhances CD8 effector/cytokine output and anti-tumor function; a top-ranked enhancer in Shifrut 2018 and a leading CAR-T knockout candidate.

tractability.assessment: hard_to_drug_small_molecule / intracellular; addressable by KO/CRISPR or gene-edited cell therapy
tractability.evidence: No ChEMBL target record (0 hits). SH2-domain adaptor — classic 'undruggable' by small molecules; being pursued as an ex vivo KO in engineered T/CAR-T cells.

genetic_evidence.anchor_disease: autoimmune / immune dysregulation (Mendelian haploinsufficiency; autoimmune GWAS at 16p13.13)
genetic_evidence.rationale: SOCS1 haploinsufficiency (heterozygous LoF) causes early-onset autoimmunity (OMIM 618287); LoF de-represses cytokine signaling. LoF -> autoimmune RISK.
genetic_evidence.interpretation_note: risk_lof scores 'discordant' under a cancer-anchored (LoF-is-protective) rule, but mechanistically CONFIRMS SOCS1 is a human immune brake whose removal amplifies T-cell activity — supportive for an IO-enhancing KO. Direction convention must be read with the disease anchor in mind.

known_drugs.note: No direct SOCS1-targeted drug; clinical translation is via SOCS1-KO engineered cell products.

active_trials.note: No small-molecule/biologic trials targeting SOCS1 directly (intracellular). Appears as an engineering KO in cell-therapy programs.

safety_flags: SOCS1 loss is pro-autoimmune (haploinsufficiency phenotype) and SOCS1 is a lymphoma tumor suppressor — durability/safety of permanent KO needs a controlled window.
